_file: The last-accepted aggregate. The §21.5 regression gate compares a run against this and nothing else.
_status: UNPOPULATED — every metric below is null. The corpus is now authored and verifies; the pipeline still cannot run end to end (chat_pipeline.answer, rerank, embed_passages, resolve_identity are all NotImplementedError), so no run has produced a number and every tolerance stays null.
_why_null: No pipeline exists yet, so no run has produced a number.
A fabricated baseline is worse than none: the first real run would be scored against an invented target,
and whichever direction it missed would be investigated as a regression that never happened.
_populating_this_file: 1. Author the fixtures (done: tools/generate_corpus.py, all ten digests real).
2. Measure the noise floor per expected/noise-floor.md. This comes BEFORE any threshold.
3. Run the suite; record the run id.
4. Copy the run's aggregate into `metrics`, its provenance into `provenance` and `judge`,
set `tolerance` from the measured spread, and fill `acceptance`.
5. Review it like any other change to a release gate.

provenance._comment: Identifies the run this baseline came from. A run that cannot be reproduced from these fields is not a baseline.
provenance._corpus_manifest_sha256: Digest over corpus/manifest.toml. Catches an edited fixture even when someone forgot to bump VERSION.
provenance._retrieval_configuration_version: The immutable §21.4 config snapshot. Defaults belong to kb-rag-query-contract and are never restated here.
provenance._source_version_pins: manifest id -> source_version_id, materialised by the seeding step. See golden/schema.md.

_comment: ADR-030: embedding and reranking are provider API calls, so the pipeline is no longer a property of the image.
Every field here can move a score with no code change, which is why each one refuses a comparison rather than
producing a delta. Built by app/evaluation/run.py's BaselineKey; a run that cannot produce one has no baseline.
_embedding_canary_digest: The measured half of embedding identity — a hash over the vectors the provider returns for a fixed in-repo probe set.
It is the ONLY detector of a vendor re-training behind an unchanged alias: the served-model string is the alias echoed
back, and cosine distance is defined between any two vectors of equal width, so nothing else moves. Never part of the
collection name; a vendor blip would then silently open a second collection instead of failing.
_rerank_applied: Reranking is CAPABILITY-GATED. Of the five providers only NVIDIA NIM exposes a ranking endpoint. A run where stage 11
was skipped served the RRF-fused order and applied NO evidence threshold at all, so its refusal rate, its packed
evidence and its faithfulness belong to a different pipeline. Such a run is recorded and reported — it is what an org
on a provider without a ranking endpoint actually experiences — and it is EXCLUDED FROM THIS BASELINE, structurally:
EvaluationRunRecord.rerank is a union whose skipped arm carries no provider, no model, no scale and no threshold, and
the only constructor of a BaselineKey raises on it. There is no value to forget to check.
One skipped case makes the whole run skipped — averaging reranked and fused cases yields a figure belonging to neither.
pipeline._rerank_skip_reason: Populated only on an ineligible run. RerankSkipReason is closed and has no member meaning the provider errored; an outage laundered into a skip degrades ranking AND hides an incident.
pipeline._rerank_scale: logit | sigmoid | unit_interval. 0.30 is a valid float on all three and means roughly opposite things; the scale travels with every score and with the threshold.
_rerank_calibration_derived_from: The evaluation run id that produced the (provider, model) threshold. There is NO portable evidence threshold any more:
app/rag/rerank.py's CALIBRATIONS is empty on purpose, and an uncalibrated model is one a bot may not threshold against.
An eval run is what PRODUCES a calibration — derive min_score as the 5th percentile of the answerable top-1 rerank
score distribution over >=50 answerable and >=50 unanswerable questions, then report the resulting false-answer rate.
Two runs against two calibrations of the same model are two experiments: the threshold IS the refusal behaviour.

judge._comment: Scores are not comparable across judge models, judge versions, or ragas versions. All of it is recorded so the gate can refuse rather than guess.
_requested_model: Must be a dated snapshot. As of 2026-08 neither of the catalogued families publishes one:
the gpt-5.6 line has no dated aliases (gpt-5.6 floats to gpt-5.6-sol) and deepseek-v4-* rolls
forward in place. Until a dated id exists, the pin is (resolved_model_id, system_fingerprint)
read back off the response, and a change in EITHER refuses the comparison. Choosing the judge
is a decision for whoever wires the first run; it needs Capability.STRUCTURED_OUTPUT.
judge._resolved_model_id: response.model, read back off the call. Never assumed equal to requested_model.
judge._system_fingerprint: The only observable that moves when the weights move under a floating alias.
judge._temperature: Set at OUR adapter. Ragas' own InstructorModelArgs default is temperature=0.01, top_p=0.1 — not zero. Temperature 0 is not deterministic at the provider either; see noise-floor.md.
judge._metrics_used: 3 judge calls per scored case: Faithfulness costs 2, ContextRecall 1. Everything else in `metrics.deterministic` costs zero LLM calls.

comparability._comment: A run failing any of these is REFUSED, not compared. The gate emits 'incomparable' and no delta.
comparability._refuse_if_differs: This list is app/evaluation/run.py's BaselineKey, field for field. A field present in one and not the other is recorded, displayed, and silently not compared — which is the worst of the three states, because it looks checked. A test asserts every BaselineKey field participates in the comparison.
comparability._refuse_if_false: A skipped-rerank run measured a different pipeline. It is recorded, never compared. This line is documentation of a property the types already enforce, not the enforcement.
comparability._refuse_if_nonzero: A run with failed judge calls is a FAILED run, not a slightly lower score. Never average over the survivors.
comparability._refuse_if_changed: A changed stale count means the question set effectively changed. That comparison is how a chunker change gets read as a prompt regression.

judged._comment: The LLM-judged half. Expensive, noisy, wide tolerance, scheduled cadence only.
_faithfulness_triple: The mean is meaningless without n and skipped, and this is not stylistic.
Ragas returns nan when statement extraction yields nothing — exactly what a refusal produces —
and np.nanmean drops those rows from the denominator. So a run with more refusals reports a
HIGHER faithfulness, and improving refusal behaviour raises the score. Refusals are skipped
explicitly, n is reported beside every mean, and the gate fails when skipped moves at all.
`errored` is separate from `skipped`: a skip is a decision, an error is a failure.
judged._context_recall_skipped: The 9 unanswerable cases carry no `reference`, so ContextRecall cannot run on them. They are SKIPPED, never scored 0. Expected skip count: 9.

deterministic._comment: Zero LLM calls, computed from retrieval_traces and citations. More actionable, cannot drift, runs on every change.

refusal._false_refusal_rate: refused AND answerable. Threshold too high. Denominator excludes the 4 clarification_ok cases that produced a clarifying question.
refusal._false_answer_rate: answered AND unanswerable. Threshold too low, or the model filled a gap from priors. Denominator is the 9 unanswerable cases.
refusal._clarification_rate: Denominator is the 4 clarification_ok cases only. Reported, never gated on alone.
refusal._crag_mean: +1 correct answer, 0 refusal, -1 wrong-or-hallucinated. The one number that moves in the right direction for both threshold failure modes.
refusal._false_answer_by_kind: Broken down by unanswerable_kind. A threshold change that trades absent_fact refusals for not_yet_published hallucinations is a different decision from a uniform improvement, and an aggregate rate hides it.

retrieval._hit_rate: Fraction of answerable cases where at least one expected source appears in the packed evidence.
retrieval._source_recall: Fraction of expected_sources retrieved, averaged over answerable cases. The metric that catches a synthesis answer built from one of two required sources.

citation._correctness: Every citation resolves to a chunk that was actually packed. Citations are assigned from retrieved evidence before generation, so anything else is a pipeline bug, not a model quirk.
citation._completeness: Every claim-bearing sentence carries a citation.

latency._note: Single-turn cases only. The 4 follow-up cases run 2 pipeline turns each and are reported separately; pooling them shifts p95 for a reason unrelated to performance.

cost._judge_calls: 3 per scored case. 37 answerable cases scored by Faithfulness + 37 with a reference for ContextRecall ≈ 111 judge calls per full run, before retries. Refusals skip both metrics, so the real count drops as the bot refuses more — budget from the answerable count, not the case count.
cost._accounting: Every judge call is a provider call: one provider_calls row, operation="evaluation.judge", the run id carried through, counted against the evaluation org's quota. Ragas' own CostCallbackHandler cannot see this path at all; metering is ours.

integrity._comment: Not quality metrics. These decide whether the run produced a publishable score at all.

_per_category: Populated with one entry per §21.2 category. An aggregate with no drill-down cannot explain a regression, which is the only moment anyone looks at it. Per-CASE detail lives in evaluation_results, not here — this file stays diffable.

tolerance._comment: Set from the MEASURED spread in expected/noise-floor.md, never guessed. A gate tighter than the noise floor fails randomly and teaches everyone to ignore it.
tolerance._method: Paired differences on the same question set with standard errors clustered by source_version_id, per arXiv:2411.00640. The gate compares intervals, not point estimates: several cases share one fixture, and treating them as independent understates the interval badly.
tolerance._faithfulness_skipped_delta: Zero, and not a measurement. Any movement in the skip count changes what the mean is a mean OF, so the two numbers cannot be compared at all. This is the one tolerance that is a rule rather than a band.

human_review._comment: §21.3 requires human review, and it is not advice. Ragas' instance-level agreement with humans is ~0.08 Pearson for faithfulness — below plain ROUGE-L. System-level ranking is usable; a single judged score is never a gate on its own.
